title: Parkinson's Law: Why Cutting Deadlines in Half Improves Quality
alt_title_1: The 1955 Naval Study That Explains Why Projects Drag On Forever
alt_title_2: Give a Task 2 Weeks vs 2 Hours (The Deadline Paradox)
description_hook: In 1955, historian C. Northcote Parkinson published a landmark essay in The Economist proving that work expands to fill whatever deadline you give it. Here is why cutting deadlines by 50% produces sharper work.

scenes.headline: Why 2-Week Tasks Take Exactly 2 Weeks
scenes.stat_label: SAME DELIVERABLE UNDER URGENCY VS COMFORT
bullets: Give a report 14 days and it bloats into 14 days
Give it 2 hours before a flight and you ship on time
scenes.narration: Give yourself two weeks to finish a project and it will mysteriously take fourteen days. Give yourself two hours before catching a flight, and you finish it with ten minutes to spare.

scenes.headline: C. Northcote Parkinson's 1955 Discovery
scenes.stat_label: THE ECONOMIST ESSAY ON BUREAUCRATIC BLOAT
bullets: British Navy warships fell 67%, yet office staff rose 78%
Work expands to fill the time available for completion
scenes.narration: In 1955, historian Cyril Northcote Parkinson proved in The Economist that as British Navy ships shrank by two-thirds, headquarters staff grew by seventy-eight percent because work expands to fill available time.

scenes.headline: Loose Deadlines Breed Fake Complexity
scenes.left_body: Tweaking fonts, opening 30 tabs, second-guessing every sentence
scenes.right_body: Forces instant focus on the 20% core that actually matters
scenes.narration: Long deadlines rarely create masterpieces; they invite perfectionism, anxious second-guessing, and decorative busywork. Tight constraints force your brain to execute only what moves the needle.

scenes.headline: Two Fast Iterations Beat One Slow Draft
scenes.stat_subtext: Version 2 after real feedback always beats Version 1 polished in a cave
scenes.narration: That is why cutting your deadline in half actually raises quality: shipping version one in three days instead of two weeks lets real feedback guide version two.

scenes.headline: Set Artificial Micro-Deadlines Today
scenes.stat_label: SHRINK THE CLOCK BEFORE STARTING ANY PROJECT
bullets: Take your top weekly goal and cut its timeline in half
Use a visible countdown timer to lock out distractions
